title: Its OK for a starter kit, the press is the only good part
text:
Its OK for a starter kit, the press is the only good part. The appeal of this kit is that it comes with everything you need (and even some stuff you don't) to see if you like the process of making French Press coffee. Honestly as a kit its ok but none of the components are all that great on their own. The burr grinder is one that I've seen before and disliked- very hard to use correctly and breaks easily. Even in the video that they show on the product page, notice how they fade to cut time when you see the user grinding. He even looks like he's struggling at first, and then the editor is like "nope, let's cut ahead some time!". The other included accessories such as the milk cup are cute, but honestly not necessary. If you have a milk frother, you're not going to pour it into this first to then pour into your coffee. And if you are using your milk straight, again, why pour it into this? For aesthetics? To serve? Maybe I'm just missing the point of it, and there aren't really instructions to clarify.
The actual press is the only part I like. Some die hards will tell you to only make it in glass but the metal container is perfectly fine IMO. The press is a little bit smaller than I'm used to, so it is only good for smaller portions of coffee, but the filter is interesting and easy to clean, which I liked.
All in all, its ok because it comes with so many things so it might make a cute gift, but I feel like you can get much higher quality versions of all the necessary components for not a lot more money. I'd rather buy a better grinder and bigger press separately, and skip the other things.
